samples.summary: Enforce-by-default turns the `attributes: null` fail-closed branch into a live denial for `CreateRevision` on any deployment that registered it and previously relied on the shadow default
samples.evidence: `decide()` still fails closed when Yorkie sends no attributes (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:254). The branch's own comment justifies this on the premise that "a would-be bypass then surfaces as a shadow-mode log before enforcement is turned on" — a premise this change removes by making enforcement the default. The repo's own integration evidence is that Yorkie sends `attributes: null` for `CreateRevision` *regardless of caller*: packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:463-479 records that the owner's own `createRevision` breaks once the method is registered. The consumer is out of diff: packages/frontend/src/components/history/use-revision-history.ts:72 and :98 call `createRevision` on every named revision and before every restore, so on a deployment that registered `CreateRevision` and left `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset, revision creation silently went from allowed (shadow) to 403 for every user. Mitigation that lowers confidence, not impact: packages/frontend/src/components/history/history-panel.tsx:133 notes deployments are told *not* to register `CreateRevision`, so the regression only bites installs that ignored that. Fix belongs either on the new default (document/handle the null-attribute RPCs) or by exempting revision-create from the fail-closed branch.

samples.summary: The new `ensureSlidesRoot({ readOnly })` gate is bypassed a few lines above it: the pending-PPTX-import `doc.update()` runs unconditionally on a read-only mount
samples.evidence: slides-view.tsx:248-274 runs `doc.update((r) => { r.meta = …; r.themes = …; r.slides = … })` when `peekPendingImport(documentId)` returns an entry, and it executes *before* the newly gated `ensureSlidesRoot(doc, { readOnly: readOnlyMount })` at :285. It is the same class of CRDT-root write the new gate exists to prevent (the diff's own rationale: a viewer's write is refused at the next PushPull and wedges their sync), and it writes far more than the seed does. `readOnlyMount` is in scope at :198, so the guard is one condition away. Reachability is what I could not confirm: the staged import is per-browser and per-documentId, so it needs the same browser to have staged a PPTX for the document it then opens through a viewer-role share link.

samples.summary: The docs package's read-only wrapper (and the docs editor) still document the webhook as shipping in shadow mode by default — the contract this change inverts; the notes twin was updated, the docs original was not
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42 states "the server-side check behind it — the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one." packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4454-4458 repeats it ("ships in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, so in a stock deployment this is the write boundary"). The new packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts explicitly corrects exactly this claim for notes and says it was wrong, but the docs files it mirrors were left describing the old default. Nested design docs repeat it too (docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:301), and the nested-doc link check does not recurse.

samples.summary: `migrateDocument`'s new meta reconciliation changes behaviour for every other consumer of the exported symbol, and now disagrees with `readMeta()`, which still uses bare `migrateMeta`
samples.evidence: `migrateDocument` is exported from packages/slides/src/index.ts:179 and node.ts:122 and is the read path of `MemSlidesStore` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:144 constructor, :156 `read()`), not just of the Yorkie store — so any deck whose `meta.themeId`/`masterId` does not appear in its own `themes`/`masters` now reads back with rewritten ids everywhere, including PPTX/export round-trips through MemSlidesStore. Meanwhile `readMeta()` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:159, packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:480, forwarded by packages/slides/src/store/layout-edit-store.ts:80) still goes through `migrateMeta` alone and therefore returns the un-reconciled `default-light`/`default` for the same document. Today's `readMeta()` callers only read `slideHeight` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1476, slides-view.tsx:972), so nothing is broken yet — but the two read paths now answer differently for themeId/masterId and the next caller that asks `readMeta()` for a theme id gets the stale one.

samples.summary: `YorkieStore`'s comment mutators changed from resolving to throwing on a read-only mount, and the sheet-view handlers that call them neither catch nor check `readOnly`
samples.evidence: `assertWritable` now throws from `addThread`/`addReply`/`editComment`/`deleteComment`/`setThreadResolved` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1321-1386). The out-of-diff callers propagate: `handleCommentResolve` (sheet-view.tsx:936-963) awaits `store?.setThreadResolved` with no try/catch and no `readOnly` guard, and `handleCommentEdit` (:967) / `handleCommentDelete` (:974) are bare awaits. They are passed straight to `CommentPopover`'s `onResolve`/`onEditComment`/`onDeleteComment` (sheet-view.tsx:1751-1753), so the only thing keeping the new rejection off the UI is the popover's freshly added `readOnly` prop — which the store's own doc comment says is "the wrong last line". A future or stale caller now gets an unhandled rejection rather than a no-op.

samples.summary: The store-level comment write gate was added to the sheets store only; the docs and PDF comment stores still rely on UI gating alone
samples.evidence: The PR's stated reason for `YorkieStore.assertWritable` is that "a UI gate is the wrong last line" (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1298-1310). The sibling CRDT comment stores have no equivalent: packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts has no `readOnly`/`assertWritable` at all (mutators at :112, :146, :164, :176, :189), and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts only remarks at :178 that "a viewer never reaches here at all — commenting is `readOnly`-gated", i.e. exactly the UI-only assurance the sheets change rejected. Both are reached today only through readOnly-gated UI (pdf-collab.tsx:378 → CommentThreadCard `readOnly`; docs-view.tsx:695), so I found no live bypass — the finding is that the invariant is now inconsistent across the three stores and the two ungated ones are the ones a future write path would use.

verdict.reason: The cited code is real (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:250-260 fails closed on empty attributes; revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:463-479,611-616 confirm Yorkie sends attributes: null for CreateRevision), but the path is unreachable in any configuration this repository produces or instructs. Auth-webhook method registration is an out-of-band `yorkie project update` action — nothing in src/, scripts, or deployment artifacts registers methods (template-review.ts:78 documents it as "a manual" step; the only --auth-webhook-method-add occurrences outside docs are in the skipped e2e spec). Both operator-facing registration commands deliberately omit CreateRevision (self-hosting.md:566-581, backend README:263) and each is followed by an explicit "Do not register CreateRevision" block (self-hosting.md:607-615, backend README:233-240, revision-history.md:148-156, frontend README:42). The "previously allowed under shadow" baseline the finding depends on is itself a forbidden posture: revision-history.md:487-493 and :504-508 state registration *plus* YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true were already release preconditions "not follow-ups", so a compliant deployment already got the 403 before the default flip and sees no change. Finally the "silently" element fails: history-panel.tsx:129-146 and :155-168 catch and render both the createRevision and restore rejections. The proposed remediation is either already implemented (documentation in four places) or would reopen an ungated CreateRevision.

finding.evidence: slides-view.tsx:248-274 runs `doc.update((r) => { r.meta = …; r.themes = …; r.slides = … })` when `peekPendingImport(documentId)` returns an entry, and it executes *before* the newly gated `ensureSlidesRoot(doc, { readOnly: readOnlyMount })` at :285. It is the same class of CRDT-root write the new gate exists to prevent (the diff's own rationale: a viewer's write is refused at the next PushPull and wedges their sync), and it writes far more than the seed does. `readOnlyMount` is in scope at :198, so the guard is one condition away. verdict.reason: The quoted code exists (slides-view.tsx:248-274 does an ungated root doc.update() before the gated ensureSlidesRoot at :285), but the path is unreachable on a read-only mount. (1) The block is wrapped in `if (documentId)` (slides-view.tsx:248), and the only mount that ever sets readOnly=true — SharedDesktopSlidesLayout at shared-document.tsx:503-508, where readOnly derives from `resolved.role === "viewer"` (shared-document.tsx:412) — does NOT pass `documentId`; the prop is optional (slides-view.tsx:47) and read nowhere else, so peekPendingImport is never called on a viewer mount. The only other SlidesView render, slides-detail.tsx:514-524, passes documentId but never passes readOnly, so readOnlyMount is false there. The shared mobile viewer mounts MobileSlidesView instead (shared-document.tsx:627). (2) Independently, nothing stages a slides pending import any more: pending-imports.ts is an in-memory Map (:19) whose setPendingImport (:21) has zero call sites in src (only slides-view.tsx:28 peeks/clears), because PPTX import now writes directly on a detached owner doc in apply-imported-content.ts:240-252. Either fact alone blocks the claimed bypass; the reviewer's own reachability premise (a "per-browser" staged import) is also incorrect. Adding `&& !readOnlyMount` would be harmless hardening but is not a blocking defect.
